days.title: Orientation and PV system overview
objectives: Orient learners to CTS Cohort 6 expectations, facilities, and daily evidence routines.
Identify the source, storage, distribution, and load blocks in a small photovoltaic system.
Apply baseline shop, electrical, battery, and tool-safety controls.
agenda: Welcome, program orientation, and workspace tour
handsOn: Complete a component-identification station rotation and assemble a labeled PV system block diagram.
safetyControls: PPE and closed-toe footwear
De-energized component handling
Battery terminal protection
Stop-work authority and housekeeping

days.title: Electricity basics and multimeter practice
objectives: Explain voltage, current, resistance, power, and energy using practical PV examples.
Configure and use a digital multimeter for safe DC measurements.
Record measurements with correct units, polarity, and reasonable-value checks.
agenda: Meter controls, leads, ranges, and ports
handsOn: Measure known sources and components, verify continuity, and document readings on the lab evidence sheet.
safetyControls: Inspect meter and leads before use
Use the correct input jack and range
Never measure resistance on an energized circuit
Maintain polarity awareness and controlled work zones
evidence: Instructor observation of safe meter setup

days.title: Wiring and crimping
objectives: Select conductors, terminals, and tools appropriate to a low-voltage PV circuit.
Strip, crimp, tug-test, and inspect repeatable terminations.
Use polarity, labeling, and continuity checks before energization.
agenda: Wire types, gauges, and connector anatomy
Crimp quality criteria and failure examples
handsOn: Produce a set of labeled sample conductors and terminal crimps that pass visual, tug, and continuity checks.
safetyControls: Eye protection during cutting and crimping
Hands clear of tool pinch points
De-energized practice boards
Control wire offcuts and sharp strands

days.title: Small solar-system build
objectives: Translate a wiring diagram into an orderly physical build.
Complete conductors and connections using verified crimping practices.
Commission a small PV system in a controlled sequence.
agenda: Continuity, polarity, staged energization, and closeout
handsOn: Build and commission a small panel-controller-battery-load system, then demonstrate expected energy flow.
safetyControls: Keep the system de-energized until preflight approval
Cover PV source during wiring
Fuse/protect source conductors
Use staged energization and a defined emergency disconnect

days.title: Commissioning, protection, voltage drop, and troubleshooting
objectives: Choose overcurrent protection and conductor size for representative DC circuits.
Calculate and interpret voltage drop.
Apply a documented commissioning and first-line troubleshooting sequence.
handsOn: Size conductors and protective devices for a scenario, commission a training circuit, and isolate seeded faults.
safetyControls: De-energize before changing conductors or protection
Use correctly rated fuses and devices
Verify polarity before energization
Apply one-change-at-a-time fault isolation

days.title: Hidden-fuse troubleshooting
objectives: Use symptoms and measurements to narrow an electrical fault.
Locate concealed or non-obvious overcurrent protection in a system path.
Explain findings with a repeatable evidence trail.
agenda: Team diagnosis, repair verification, and debrief
handsOn: Diagnose a non-operational training system containing a hidden-fuse fault and verify restored operation.
safetyControls: Treat unknown circuits as energized until verified
Measure before opening enclosures
Replace only with the specified fuse rating
No bypassing protective devices

days.title: Load assessment and system sizing
objectives: Inventory loads and calculate daily energy demand.
Apply autonomy, system-loss, battery-depth-of-discharge, and solar-production assumptions.
Propose a coherent PV, storage, controller, inverter, and conductor sizing concept.
handsOn: Complete a residential or mobile load assessment and develop a traceable preliminary system-sizing package.
safetyControls: Use nameplate data and approved assumptions
Separate AC and DC calculation paths
Flag uncertain loads rather than guessing
Keep design activity de-energized

days.title: Final review and assessment
objectives: Integrate PV system concepts, measurement, wiring, protection, commissioning, and sizing.
Demonstrate safe, systematic practical work.
Submit a complete evidence package and identify next-step growth areas.
agenda: Evidence audit, feedback, and course closeout
handsOn: Complete the PV101 written and practical assessments, including inspection, measurement, diagnosis, and explanation.
safetyControls: Follow every station's energization state
Use PPE and verified meter setup
Stop on unexpected conditions
Instructor approval before resets or rewiring
